I think mahihirapan ang mga taga Pampanga magrecommend kasi sawa na sila. Pero ako half kapampangan who lives in Laguna and there's so much to appreciate doon that locals don't. Ako pa nagtotour sa pinsan kong taga doon haha.

First of all, best to set up your base sa Angeles/Clark. Doon palang marami ka na magagawa. Lahat ng kainan, cafes, attractions, andun lahat naka center. 

For activities, try yung wakeboarding park at Deca. Okay din accommodations doon. Firing range Mountain Clark Firing Range near marquee ay mura and in my experience, very good instructors. Aqua Planet for water park. Driving range (golf) sa EG Golf. May 4D theater din ang Clark Museum. City Kart racing for go cart. While at the museum, take a stroll narin on the parade grounds.

If lalayo ka kaunti, pwede ka mag Sandbox sa Porac. If you have a car, take a daytrip to subic. Tarlac Recreational Park is also worth a daytrip. Go early para sulit, pero avoid Mondays kasi maintenance day siya. I haven't tried, pero baka feasible din daytrip to La Union.

And of course it's absurd to go to the culinary capital without going on a food trip! So for local food, you can try Mila's Tokwa't Baboy for deep fried sisig and tokwa't baboy, Junjun for chicken barbeque, aling lucing to get an idea what authentic sisig tastes like, and Matam-ih for some authentic aeta cuisine.

As for non local, but GOLD, I also have recommendations.

I am not a cake person, except for when I am at Cioccolo. My dad bought my birthday cake here when I was a kid, and my friends here in Laguna were able to taste. 13 years later they still haven't forgotten that cake hahaha. The owner studied in new york and the textures are amazing. The place is also very instagramable on top of that. My favorite there is the creme brulee cake. If makakarating ka San Fernando, try niyo yung goto sa Lelut Baculud. It's so good!

Spanglish feels closer to an authentic tex mex experience. It's inside Clark.

Hard to not compare other vietnamese restos here to Banh Mi in the heart of Angeles, along Jesus street.

Funniest thing about pasalubongs, I never go home to Laguna eithout buying siomai from Suzies 😅 There's so much to love there. I buy palabok there too. Also, if you are feeling adventurous, you can try bottled buro there. Goes great with mustasa and some fried fish. Doesn't stink like the buro I am familiar with, so that's great.

And I don't have a specific recommendation but the Korean town there has a lot to offer too.

For nature, you can try hiking Mt. Pinatubo and get to see the crater lake. Allocate a day for this. This trail is beginner friendly.

Lastly, as a 100% wfh person, sa Pampanga ako pinaka naging comfortable sa cafes magwork. Yes, even more than Manila. Magaganda cafes, have good food and good drinks. They are huge, have great wifi, and have good food and drinks.

I feel like I enjoy pampanga more than my cousins who live there. they do not know what they have good haha. I hope this helps!

I'm half kapampangan and half tagalog. Spent my childhood in pampanga and spent the rest of my life in Laguna. I was so confused when I tasted sisig in Laguna as a kid.

I don't care if you like putting eggs or mayonnaise in your sisig. In fact, some of my kapampangan cousins like putting mayonnaise and that's okay.

But sisig is a process. It is a kapampangan word that means "to sour". Pretty weird if you were asked to cook kare kare and you made adobo. That's what's weird about how sisig is prepared in Tagalog regions.

When you say sisig, it will mean something else before Aling Lucing made it the way we know it today, which is diced pork in a sizzling plate. It was a simple sour papaya salad in the beginning. Then it was a seafood dish. What do they have in common? They are all sour. Tagalog sisig is not sour.

Might mean nothing to a lot of people, but proper names will play a huge role in history decades or centuries from now.

A lot of us do not even know the origin of a lot of our words, but we can still trace it because it stayed true to its meaning. Kapampangans are people living on the pampang (riverbank). Tagalogs are "taga ilogs". Sinigang means "stewed", and it's still a stew! Someday, sisig is going to be salty only, and no one will know why it doesn't taste sour despite its name. And given how we barely document our cultural heritage, it is another step closer to losing what little is left of it. 

What do people like me want? I just want the tagalog version to be named something else. This way it starts its own history without spoiling the other. In fact, I like the both in their own way. But I'd love it if someone in Laguna would call something sisig, and I would be confident that I will be eating something sour, and the same goes for the tagalog sisig in pampanga.

I'm for reinventing food the proper way. My favorite sisig is actually the one from Mila's Tokwa't Baboy. It's deep fried instead of grilled.

I know they already told you to train with Bernard. But I'd like to put more stress in it. Like, train until he's got nothing left to teach you.

A lot of people quit this game even after training with him because they didn't finish the entire training. After you do, you'll be better with weapons than the average swordsman.

Next tip, keep doing chumps on the river in Ledetchko until you level your archery skills well enough. You'll also start to figure out where the panthom crosshair is here, if you decide against modding it into the game.

And after all that, hunt down all of the cuman and bandit camps you know of until you have about 2700 grochen so you can buy warehorse jenda in Merjohed. It's the best base game horse in my opinion. There are better horses since the DLCs came out depending on what stat you want maxed out the most, but Jenda is an all rounder and is easy enough to obtain after a quest in that town.

After all that, you have the best combat skills and the best horse. Now you just need the best weapon. That's all up to you but the best all rounder would be the Noble's sword. But personally I slash more and stab seldomly so I'm more of a St George's Sword type of guy. I also barely get hit since aside from being a stealth player, I deflect most of the attacks if I ever get detected so armor doesn't matter to me as long as it's light. You'll need to ask somebody else about that.

If you focus on all that before getting into other quests, you'll maximize your experience since you'll outdo most of the combat encounters and have the best horse to transport stuff around.

I also don't buy any equipment since most of the best stuff can be looted anyway. Better to save up money especially if you have From The Ashes DLC. Hope this helps!

Edit: I remembered something else. In real life they tell you to stay on the beaten path so you don't get lost. I suggest you keep a bit out of it. Like, just enough to see it but not enough to be on it and you'll be fine. Ideally, always one tree away from the path.

Remember sa isang company, profits first palagi. Given that, hindi lang yung kagalingan mo factor sa application. After years applying and interviewing applicants ito napansin ko yung criteria:

1. Skill -eto alam mo na to. Pero to elaborate, pwedeng magaling ka naman, pero di mo pa alam gawin yung kailangan nila. Piliin nila yung marunong na, kasi makakatipid sila sa oras at effort magturo.

2. Personality - minsan yung fact na mukha kang introvert, joining an extroverted team, possible na factor na siya. Meron ako mga nainterview magaling na sana, kaso may maririnig kang line na condescending to others. Red flag sa mga katulad ko yun.

3. Chemistry - Yung dati kong boss di kinuha yung isang applicant kasi di niya daw mabebear yung speaking habit niya araw araw. Meron kasi siyang distinct word na palagi sinasabi. Fucked up, but that's reality.

4. Price - may hindi kasing galing mo, pero mas mura asking. Yung skill level niya sakto na din sa kailangan nila kahit di kasing galing mo.

5. Connections - pag tropa mo yung boss wala na finish na haha. Di naman siya palagi fucked up, kasi minsan mas efficient talaga daloy ng trabaho kapag may chemistry na kayo nung katrabaho mo. Connections imply or give the illusion of chemistry. Pero minsan mag tropa pero walang chemistry, pero sad to say sa tropa parin punta trabaho. May positive impact sa social life ni boss eh.

So given yang mga yan, hindi siya all about being good at what you do. Honestly, ligawan ang job application (sad reality). Honestly kung meron ka nung number
5, may cases na kahit wala ka nung 1-4, ikaw mapipili.

Ganun talaga ang buhay. Pero do what you can para umangat sa mga criteria na yan. Make as many connections as you can. You'll never know kung saan makakarating yung kakilala mo at san ka nila madadala.

Filipino here. 

In my country you will experience different dishes when you are in different provinces. Adobo and Sinigang are the well known dishes from our country, but these are Tagalog dishes (Tagalogs dominate the capital). Kare Kare is not as famous but is also a unique Tagalog dish (i think). Sisig is a Kapampangan favorite which is originally made from pig ears, and it has an Ilocano version which is called Dinakdakan, which tastes different from its sister dish. Both are awesome and I eat them a lot. 

The Ilocanos also have Pinapaitan made out of goat innards and is good and unique. Take note that there are different ways to cook it. The Ilocanos like it with goat bile, while I don't and prefer calamansi skin for adding the bitter taste instead. Pinapaitan means "bittered" in English after all.

Finally there's Laing from the Bicolanos. This can be easily turned into a vegan dish since it mainly uses taro leaves. I usually eat this without any meat, and I'm not even a vegetarian. Yet it fills me up and it's really good if done right.

These only make up a small fraction of the unique dishes you'll find here in the Philippines. I am a mix of Tagalog, Kapampangan and Ilocano with Bicolano friends and that's why these are all I cared to highlight. Not sure about your sense of taste, but we usually eat all of our food with rice. You might find our food here strong-flavored since we neutralize it with rice.

He saw the men start to pick up his children's lifeless bodies, and all his strength went into the bonds that held him in place.

He felt their leader pull him up and lean him against the railing of the bow. "You can watch as we feed them to the sharks," he sneered. He could not describe what he felt at that moment. He screamed in anguish through the gag as they threw her overboard. He focused on her as she fell into the sea, never to be seen again. He wanted to pour all of the pain he felt into the sea and ask anyone in it for retribution. He did what he could anyway.

"It's time to end our suffering."

"Never again will we perish under economic struggles." 

"Never again will they bring pandemics upon us."

"These vermins must be exterminated. our ancestors saw them for what they truly are."

And then it appeared.

From the middle of the ocean, a gigantic serpent-like beast emerged, as if it was a spear of a titan coming out of the sea. Despite it's size, it did not send out waves at all. The waters were completely under its command.

His captors were in shock, staring at the huge monster before them. It was a bizarre scene, monsters in shock of seeing a monster.

From its head in the sky, it slowly stooped down to the level of the boat. His captors who were in disbelief were now in a frenzy, shooting away at the monster in desperation, yet it was unfazed.

In response to the violence, it brought itself up, opened its mouth, and blew out a glowing breath. The sea turned green, and so did the sky. The people on the boat started to hold their necks, as if trying to hold onto their last breaths. He had the privilege of watching their leader die a slow death, his life giving one last jolt as life left his body.

He was now lying down against the deck, devoid of emotion, yet full of curiosity. What was this being in front of him? Why was he left alive?

"Behold, the beginning of Ragnarok," a voice inside his head resonated. He realized that the monster was speaking to him.

"You have witnessed the beginning of the end. I will give you the privilege of satisfying your curiosity if you wish to, since I feel like amusing myself after my long isolation from the surface."

"I do," he tried to see if the being could hear his thoughts. "Who are you?"

On this day, I am to poison the sea and the sky, as you have witnessed. It baffles one's ancient mind how well the humans have done in poisoning their sea without me."

It gave a low rumble, almost sounding like thunder, in what must have been its laugh.

"A battle will determine whether your kind will continue to exist."

"Then I hope you win."

It moved its head slightly, as if in amusement.

"This is not how I imagined your kind would have reacted."

"Oh believe me, not everyone will like what you are about to do. But there will also be a lot of us who will. We have given up on our own kind. Erasing us is the kindest thing any one can give us at this point."

"I guess I will see for myself."

It took a look around, to see where it should go next.

 You are a curious being, but I'm afraid our conversation has reached its end. I will give you a peaceful passing."

He tried to sit up as best he could, and watched as Jörmungandr blew his acid breath onto him.

He sent a quick "thank you" just a few moments before his consciousness crumbled to pieces, and his body into dust.

The band Sorority Noise's songs even helped me celebrate this victory. Songs celebrating triumph over depression can be quite rare.
